title: Compact Fully Integrated Alignment-Free and Linearly Polarized Ho$^{3+}$ Single-Frequency Waveguide Laser
authors: Jeswin Jacob, T Toney Fernandez, Dale Otten, Ori Henderson-Sapir, 3 Karen Privat, David Lancaster
abstract: We report, for the first time, a fully integrated Ho$^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass waveguide laser incorporating a femtosecond laser-inscribed waveguide and waveguide Bragg grating. The compact 12.4 mm cavity achieves stable single-frequency lasing at 2062.21 nm with a line width of better than 5 MHz. The laser emits linearly polarized light, which is efficiently delivered through an SM1950 single-mode fiber. This alignment-free architecture provides a compact and robust platform for integrated mid-infrared single-frequency laser sources.
summary: This paper reports the creation of a highly compact, integrated, and alignment-free single-frequency laser source operating in the mid-infrared using $	ext{Ho}^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass. By integrating femtosecond laser-written waveguides and Bragg gratings, the authors achieved stable lasing at $2062.21 	ext{ nm}$ with excellent spectral purity and linear polarization. This platform offers a robust alternative to traditional bulk laser sources for quantum applications.
main_problem: The primary goal was to develop a compact, fully integrated, alignment-free, and linearly polarized single-frequency laser source operating in the mid-infrared using $	ext{Ho}^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated stable single-frequency lasing at $2062.21 	ext{ nm}$ with a narrow linewidth ($< 5 	ext{ MHz}$) and confirmed linear polarization, all within a compact, integrated chip architecture.
method: The system was fabricated by inscribing waveguides and waveguide Bragg gratings (WBGs) into fluoride glass using a femtosecond laser, followed by characterization of lasing performance and polarization state.
model_or_system: The physical system is an $	ext{Ho}^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass waveguide laser cavity. The cavity is formed by integrating a femtosecond laser-inscribed waveguide and a WBG, creating a compact, chip-scale resonator.
key_observables: Lasing wavelength ($2062.21 	ext{ nm}$), linewidth ($< 5 	ext{ MHz}$), polarization state (linear), spectral bandwidth ($	ext{FWHM}$), and coupling coefficient ($\kappa$).
important_parameters: Mid-infrared range ($\sim 2 \mu	ext{m}$), waveguide width ($\approx 9 \mu	ext{m}$), and grating lengths ($5 	ext{ to } 13.5 	ext{ mm}$).
main_assumptions: The alignment-free nature is attributed to the butt-coupling of the pump light via the PR grating, and polarization selectivity is hypothesized to arise from form birefringence or polarization-dependent scattering losses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (waveguide/grating placement), spectral measurements (transmission/reflection of gratings), and time-domain measurements showing stable lasing output and polarization analysis.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication process using femtosecond laser inscription, characterizes the resulting Bragg grating resonances, demonstrates stable single-frequency lasing, and investigates the underlying physics governing polarization selectivity.
why_interesting: This work represents an advanced demonstration of integrated photonics in the mid-IR, which is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum communication applications that require stable, compact sources.
